title: Video 4 · What if your best day counted twice?
subtitle: Booster Card: what it is, why we built it, how much it adds and when to save it · script from the team (word for word) · recordings IMG_7404 (Booster), IMG_7406 (Capping) · 12 slides · voice: Tara, stability 0, one take after approval

beats.vo: What if your best day counted twice? That's the Booster Card.
flags: Type: explainer. The script explains what the Booster Card is, why it was built and its rules (15,000 cap, deficit limit, past days only). That's more "why" than "tap", so it isn't a walkthrough.

F1 intro: the headline follows the voice, from "Best day, counted twice?" to "The Booster Card" (at "Booster"). A Day 40 card comes in at 15,000 (gold, capped) and lifts to 30,000 with the rocket badge on "twice". This is the same pattern as Video 1's 4,200 → 10,000.
Day 40 "before" value: the recording only shows Day 40 after the boost (30,000). The 15,000 "before" comes from the app's own message ("You've done 21545 steps, but your contest cap is 15,000").

Length: about 85–95 s (estimate at Tara's pace). That's over the 75 s explainer guideline. The script is kept word for word, so cutting is your call. The easiest cut is the "active all week / desk on weekdays" line (~11 s).

Section cards (E3) left out: design.md wants long explainers marked with voiced E3 "PART n OF 3" cards, but the script has no lines for them and the video is already long. If you want them, approve or reword: "First, why did we build it?" / "So how does it work?" / "And when should you save it?" (+~10 s).
Scene types (5): E14, E5, E12, C5 and C3, plus the F1/F2 cards and three phone slides. No scene runs twice in a row.
Voice: Tara, stability 0, eleven_v4. The whole script goes out as one take, generated once, after you approve the wording (including the "Pick your best one" question).

beats.vo: Koshiqa is about building a habit of movement. One you can sustain, with no pressure.
flags: E14 (a week, a habit): the line draws into a 7-day streak of gently varied humps. "A habit of movement" appears on "habit", then "No pressure" on "pressure".

beats.vo: But everyone's routine is different. Some members are active all week, moving around at work. Others are stuck at a desk on weekdays, and find their weekends for a morning run or a workout.
flags: E5 (a trend against a target): one week's chart with low weekdays under the 10K goal line and two big weekend peaks, labelled "Weekend run". The values are illustrative, not from an account.
Choice: the chart shows the desk-worker week only. The "active all week" member is in the voice only, which keeps one focal point. Say if you want both routines shown side by side instead.

beats.vo: So members asked us: can we make the best use of our best days? Can my weekend cover for my weekdays?
flags: E12 list of the two questions: "Use our best days?" and "Weekend covers weekdays?", each landing as it's spoken.

No chat screen here: Video 1's chat mockup needs a real member message with consent. This line is a summary of what members asked, so it's shown as a list. If there's a real message you can share, it can become a chat like Video 1's.

beats.vo: So we built the Booster Card. You can apply it on any past day. Pick your best one.
flags: From IMG_7404 (0:11): the Power card screen. The name shows first (titleFirst), then the phone rises, a ring lands on the Booster card on "Booster Card", and the cursor taps it on "Pick".

⚠ Fact check: "Pick your best one". The app says the card "Finds your best step day automatically", and the recording applies it straight to Nov 13 ("Boosting your strongest day…") with no step to choose a day. Should the line stay as written (it reads as advice), or change to match the app, e.g. "It picks your best one for you"? A change would mean one re-take of this line only.

beats.vo: The contest counts up to 15,000 steps a day. Booster doubles those counted steps.
flags: From IMG_7404 (0:14): the Booster Card screen. The phone zooms in on the 15,000 → 30,000 boxes on "15,000", then the 30,000 box is ringed on "doubles".
Recording vs script: the green banner on this screen says "You've done 21545 steps". The script's example is 18,000, but it's on the next slide, so this slide only uses the boxes.

beats.vo: Did 18,000 steps? 15,000 count, and Booster adds another 15,000.
flags: C5 bar (part + bonus = total), as in Videos 1 and 2: "Did 18,000" day, 15,000 counted steps rise first, then the Booster bonus stacks 15,000 on top, then "15,000 + 15,000 = 30,000" is held about 10 s. The headline lands with the total.
Number not in the script: C5 always writes out the total. 30,000 follows from the script (15,000 + 15,000) and matches Day 40 in the recording.

beats.vo: But it only covers what you're behind. If your deficit is 10,000 steps, Booster adds 10,000 steps.
flags: E12 with two items: "Deficit: 10,000" on "deficit", then "Booster adds 10,000" on "adds". It's a second E12 (after "Members asked"), with three slides in between, to stay within 5 scene types.

beats.vo: No deficit, or a very small one? Save your Booster for when it counts. Any day with 15,000 steps or more gives you the full boost.
flags: C3 compare: left (✗) "No or small deficit" → "Save it", on "No deficit"; right (✓) "15,000+ day" → "Full boost", on "Any day".
Headline: "Save it till it counts" is shortened from "Save your Booster for when it counts" to fit 4 words. It could also be "When it counts".

beats.vo: And it's for past days only. For days ahead, there's Capping.
flags: From IMG_7406 (0:07): the Capping Card screen. The line "Raises your daily limit to 25,000 steps for one future day" is ringed on "days ahead". The rest of IMG_7406 (scheduling a capping day) isn't used, since the script only names Capping. Capping could get its own video.

beats.vo: Some days you hit it out of the park, while others are normal.
flags: E14 with uneven humps: the tall ones rise on "park" and the low ones on "normal". It's the same scene as slide 2, at the other end of the video.

beats.vo: Make the best use of your best days with booster cards.
flags: F2 closing with Torty winking. On screen it reads "Booster Card" (capitalised); the voice reads the script as written.
